grammar_rules.summary: List of verbs not followed by a preposition before an infinitive.
grammar_rules.explanation: Certain French verbs are followed directly by an infinitive without any preposition. When the subjects of the two verbs differ, a que clause is used instead.
usage: After the listed verbs when the same subject performs both actions.
restrictions: Subject of first verb must be same as subject of infinitive; otherwise use que clause.
conditions: The main verb is one that takes no preposition before an infinitive (vouloir, pouvoir, devoir, aimer, etc.).
The subject of the first verb is the same as the subject of the infinitive; otherwise a que clause is used.
exceptions: When the two subjects differ, a que-clause replaces the infinitive
No preposition (à or de) is inserted after these verbs
agreement_rules: The conjugated verb agrees with its subject in person and number; the infinitive carries no agreement.
When the subjects differ, a que clause is used and its verb agrees with its own subject.
common_traps: Do not insert à or de after these verbs.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Infinitive after expressions of spending time
grammar_rules.summary: After expressions like passer son temps à, gaspiller sa vie à, the infinitive is used with preposition à.
grammar_rules.explanation: The preposition à links the time expression to the infinitive.
usage: To describe how time is spent.
restrictions: Only with expressions such as passer son temps, passer ses vacances, gaspiller sa vie, perdre son temps
The preposition à must precede the infinitive; de is not used
conditions: An expression of spending time is used (passer son temps, perdre son temps, gaspiller sa vie).
The infinitive that follows is preceded by à.
exceptions: à cannot be replaced by de
Limited to expressions such as passer son temps and gaspiller sa vie
agreement_rules: The infinitive is invariable and never agrees
The conjugated verb of the expression agrees with its subject
common_traps: Do not omit the preposition à.

grammar_rules.summary: The infinitif présent can be used as the subject of a verb, corresponding to English gerund or present participle.
grammar_rules.explanation: In French, the infinitive is often used where English uses -ing form as subject.
usage: To express an action as the subject of a sentence.
restrictions: Applies only when the infinitive functions as the subject of the verb
Not used where French requires a present participle (participe présent)
conditions: The action functions as the subject of the sentence.
French uses the infinitif présent where English uses a gerund.
exceptions: The present participle is not used as a subject in French
The infinitive remains invariable and does not agree with anything
agreement_rules: The infinitive is invariable and takes no subject agreement
The main verb is third-person singular when the infinitive is its subject
grammar_rules.word_order: Infinitive at beginning of sentence as subject.
transformations: English gerund subject -> French infinitive subject
common_traps: Do not use present participle in French for subject; use infinitive.

sources.section_title: The infinitif présent
sources.source_text: The infinitif can be used as the subject of a verb. (Note that the present participle is used in English instead.)

grammar_rules.summary: The infinitive is used for general instructions, prescriptions, public notices, and proverbs.
grammar_rules.explanation: In French, the infinitive often replaces the imperative in formal or impersonal instructions.
restrictions: Modern household magazines tend to use imperative, but infinitive is used in professional contexts.
conditions: The text is a general instruction, prescription, public notice, recipe, or proverb.
The infinitive is used impersonally instead of a conjugated imperative form.
exceptions: Modern household magazines tend to use the imperative instead
The infinitive stays invariable and is never conjugated for a subject
agreement_rules: The infinitive stays invariable and is never conjugated
The object after the infinitive keeps its own gender and number
common_traps: Do not conjugate the infinitive; keep it invariant.

sources.section_title: Infinitive for instructions and notices
sources.source_text: The infinitif is also used for general instructions, prescriptions, public notices, and proverbs

grammar_rules.summary: Negation ne...pas precedes the infinitive and is not separated.
grammar_rules.explanation: Because the infinitive is not conjugated, the negative elements are placed before the infinitive as a unit.
restrictions: Applies only to a non-conjugated infinitive
ne and pas remain together before the infinitive and are never split around it
conditions: The verb to negate is in the infinitive.
Ne and pas precede the infinitive together and are not separated.
exceptions: ne and pas form a unit before the infinitive and are never split
With a conjugated verb, ne and pas normally surround the verb instead
agreement_rules: The infinitive carries no person or number agreement, so ne pas + infinitive stays invariable in form.
ne and pas are invariable negative particles and do not agree with the subject.
transformations: Il a décidé de ne pas partir.
common_traps: Do not place ne before and pas after the infinitive.

sources.section_title: Negation with infinitive
sources.source_text: the negation (ne… pas) does not surround the verb but rather precedes it, and is not separated.

grammar_rules.summary: List of verbs requiring de before a following infinitive.
grammar_rules.explanation: These verbs are followed by de + infinitive; must be memorized.
restrictions: The preposition de is required; à is not possible with these verbs
The list must be memorized because the choice is not predictable from meaning
de becomes d' before a vowel
conditions: The main verb is one that requires de (choisir de, finir de, avoir peur de, etc.).
An infinitive follows the preposition de.
exceptions: The preposition de is required; à is not possible with these verbs
de becomes d' before a vowel
agreement_rules: The main verb agrees with its subject in person and number; the infinitive carries no agreement.
The preposition de is invariable and introduces the dependent infinitive.
common_traps: Do not confuse with à verbs.

à contracts with the definite article (au, aux) when followed by a noun
